cards.explanation: The answer is the chief priests and Jewish leaders, friends. Festus, who took over after Felix (Acts 24:27), barely gets settled in the province before they present their case against Paul (Acts 25:1-2). Some folks wait for a housewarming gift. These folks brought a legal case.

The answer is to ambush and kill Paul on the way. The text says it plainly: the leaders were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way (Acts 25:3). So that "concession" they asked for wasn't a friendly favor. I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story, friends.

The answer is that they should come down with Festus and accuse Paul there. Festus says, "…let some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him there." (Acts 25:5) He's not moving Paul anywhere, friends. If they want a case, the case comes to Caesarea, where Paul is already being held.
The answer is Paul. Festus sits on the judgment seat and orders that Paul be brought in (Acts 25:6). He does it the next day after going down to Caesarea, friends.

The answer is that Paul has committed no offense. Paul says, "I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar." (Acts 25:8) Notice he covers all three bases, friends: the law, the temple and Caesar. The accusers couldn't prove their charges, and Paul stays steady.

The answer is True, friends. The text says Festus, "…wishing to do the Jews a favor…" asks Paul, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges?" (Acts 25:9) Festus had told the leaders earlier that Paul was staying in Caesarea. Now he's asking Paul about going up to Jerusalem.

The answer is before the judgment seat of Caesar. Paul says, "I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried." (Acts 25:10) He also adds that he has done nothing wrong to the Jews, as Festus himself knows very well. Paul isn't asking for a favor here, friends. He's saying where the trial belongs.

The answer is True. Paul says, "If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die." (Acts 25:11) He isn't dodging punishment if he's guilty, friends. He goes on to say that if there is no truth to their accusations, no one has the right to hand him over to them.

The answer is False. Festus confers with his council and then replies, "You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!" (Acts 25:12) He accepts the appeal, friends. Paul asked for Caesar and Caesar is what he gets.
